value.body: Some chartered accountants add a second professional qualification: Company Secretary (ICSI), which focuses on corporate law, governance and compliance, or Cost and Management Accountant (ICMAI), which focuses on costing, cost audit and management accounting. Both institutes give qualified CAs some credit for their prior study.

items.label: CS route
items.note: Passed CA Final candidates are exempt from CSEET (an exemption fee applies)

items.label: CMA route
items.note: Foundation not required for graduates and CA candidates

items.label: Bodies
items.note: Both are statutory bodies under Acts of Parliament

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Register with ICSI or ICMAI using your CA qualification for direct entry, complete the remaining papers and the required training, and apply for membership. Paper-wise exemptions change with syllabus revisions, so check the institute's current rules.

value.title: At a glance
items: A CS adds value for work in secretarial, listing and corporate-law compliance; it is needed to act as a company secretary.
A CMA adds value for cost audit and costing-heavy industry roles.
It takes extra years alongside work, so many add it only when their role needs it.
